entries.title: Our galaxy’s supermassive black hole actually doesn’t devour everything
entries.content:
Inside almost every known galaxy lurks a [supermassive black hole](https://www.popsci.com/category/black-holes/), and our home [Milky Way](https://www.popsci.com/science/new-milky-way-image-euclid-telescope/) galaxy is no exception. Located about 26,000 light-years from Earth, [Sagittarius A\*](https://www.popsci.com/science/nasa-chandra-back-catalog/) anchors millions of stars and their planets with its incomprehensibly gargantuan gravitational pull. But after reviewing recent observations made by NASA’s [James Webb Space Telescope](https://www.popsci.com/tag/jwst/) (JWST), astronomers discovered that some material can exist closer to a galactic black hole than previously believed. Despite existing just 0.55 light-years from Sagittarius A\*, the ancient star known as IRS 3 is shooting out immense stellar winds while surrounded by oxygen-rich dust and even water.

“Galactic centers are among the most extreme environments, so understanding whether stars can continue enriching their surroundings there is an important question,” [said Florian Peißker](https://esawebb.org/news/weic2617/), an astronomer at Germany’s University of Cologne and the co-author of a paper on the discovery published today in the journal [*Astronomy and Astrophysics*](https://www.aanda.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202660243).

![This image showcases the location of the highly evolved star IRS 3, which is located just 0.55 light-years from Sagittarius A*, the Milky Way galaxy's central supermassive black hole. The images show a progressinvely closer view of the region using ground- and space-based data. An international team of astronomers have discovered that dust and water can form and survive surprisingly close to this supermassive black hole. The observations reveal that the evolved star IRS 3 continues to enrich its surroundings with newly formed material despite the intense radiation environment around Sagittarius A*.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IRS3-Photos.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

This image showcases the location of the highly evolved star IRS 3, which is located just 0.55 light-years from Sagittarius A\*, the Milky Way galaxy’s central supermassive black hole. The images show a progressinvely closer view of the region using ground- and space-based data. An international team of astronomers have discovered that dust and water can form and survive surprisingly close to this supermassive black hole. The observations reveal that the evolved star IRS 3 continues to enrich its surroundings with newly formed material despite the intense radiation environment around Sagittarius A\*. *Credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/E. Slawik/M. Zamani, ESO/S. Guisard, NASA/JPL-Caltech/S. Stolovy (Spitzer Science Center/Caltech), F. Peißker, J. Lu*

Stellar deaths are vital parts of the galactic life cycle. As a star begins to die, it sheds waves of gas into space that later form the foundations of [cosmic dust](https://www.popsci.com/science/cosmic-dust-origin-of-life/). In turn, this space dust becomes the building blocks for planets and other celestial objects. The star at the center of our galaxy’s black hole, IRS 3, is a perfect example of these interactions. After 72 million years of existence, IRS 3 has entered its asymptotic giant branch phase, making it bright, cool, and about six times the sun’s mass. Astronomers have long known IRS 3 should hypothetically emit gas along its stellar winds, but they were unsure if that was even possible given its proximity to Sagittarius A\*.

Previous data indicated IRS 3’s large dust envelope implied that the star was rich in carbon, but JWST has supplied evidence to the contrary. Using its [Mid-Infrared Instrument](https://www.popsci.com/science/jwst-cosmic-tornado/) (MIRI), researchers detected two strong signatures that align with silicate dust made from oxygen and silicon. This means that IRS 3 possesses a lot of oxygen as it nears the end of its life.

The team used advanced simulation models to test how radiated light might move through different types of surrounding cosmic dust envelopes. The astronomers then used those models to build a theoretical structure of IRS 3’s actual envelope. They now believe the elderly star is surrounded by a layered shell of cosmic dust spanning about 0.15 light-years in every direction. Temperatures near the star hover around 1,700 degrees Fahrenheit, while the outer layers average about -280 Fahrenheit. For the first time, researchers also noted clear signs of water within the envelope of a star like IRS 3.

European Space Agency (ESA) astronomer [Macarena Garcia Marin](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Macarena-Garcia-Marin) described the discovery as “especially exciting,” because it indicates foundational molecular material like water can still exist in intensely hostile, irradiated environments.

“This tells us that even close to a supermassive black hole, stars can continue contributing material back into their surroundings,” she added.

The post [Our galaxy’s supermassive black hole actually doesn’t devour everything](https://www.popsci.com/science/milky-way-black-hole-water-dust/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: China’s experimental bullet train hits 497 mph in 5 seconds
entries.content:
A nearly 2,550-pound, experimental [maglev train car](https://www.popsci.com/technology/self-driving-bullet-train/) in China recently has beat its own short-distance acceleration world record for the third time in six months. But while it reached 0 to 497 miles in 5.3 seconds, don’t expect to climb aboard something similar to the [Donghu Laboratory vehicle](https://interestingengineering.com/transportation/china-maglev-speed-record) anytime soon. Instead, its uses may align more with advanced rocketry and military capabilities.

Maglev trains are,[unfortunately, nowhere to be found](https://www.popsci.com/technology/amtrak-bullet-train-texas/) in the United States.They’ve remained a major form of transportation for decades across China, Japan, and parts of Europe. The rides [safely ferry passengers](https://www.popsci.com/technology/high-speed-trains-hyperloop-history/) at upwards of 200 mph with a specialized system of magnetic coils that generate alternating electromagnetic fields. Once engaged, the magnetic currents both levitate and rapidly accelerate the train forward towards its next stop, allowing it to bypass the friction constraints of standard locomotive travel.

The world’s fastest commercial maglev train is the Fuxing rail in China, which reaches a top speed of 217 mph while averaging 197 mph along its 635-mile-long track. However, Donghu Laboratory is experimenting with immensely more power systems. Their first public run of the test vehicle in June 2025 reached about 404 mph in 7.1 seconds, establishing the first world record for short-distance maglev acceleration. That July, engineers boosted the top speed to 433 mph before doing so again to 496 mph in November. These trials confirmed multiple new [underlying technological advances](https://interestingengineering.com/transportation/china-maglev-speed-record) including high-power energy delivery, levitation control, positioning, electromagnetic propulsion, and emergency braking.

Precision is at a major premium to safely reach these acceleration benchmarks. A 2,550-pound train car is hefty at rest, meaning incredible amounts of force and energy are required to shove it to such high speeds within a matter of seconds. The experimental train is comparatively lightweight at those velocities, which means track deviations are limited to within only 0.5 millimeters. Control systems must also ensure similarly accurate positioning to keep the vehicle within its operating parameters.

These speeds (and their accompanying 2.9 G’s of acceleration) may never be experienced on a standard maglev commuter ride, however. Given overall infrastructure costs, energy requirements, and safety concerns, engineers imagine similar technologies will instead find uses for rocketry and military aircraft. For example, adapting the system to rapidly accelerate cargo rockets, drones, and other planes ahead of takeoff could dramatically reduce onboard fuel requirements. Other maglev systems could wind up in industrial transport systems and elevators.

While aircraft-speed ground transportation may not be imminent, today’s maglev rails remain plenty fast, economical, and safe. For now, most people in the U.S. would still settle for at least one traditional bullet train route.

The post [China’s experimental bullet train hits 497 mph in 5 seconds](https://www.popsci.com/technology/fastest-experimental-bullet-train-china/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: ‘It’s going to be spectacular’: Millions flock to Spain seeking best view of total solar eclipse
entries.content:
Eclipse chasers, tourists and astronomers searching for the clearest skies to watch the two minutes of totality

The online forums are abuzz as people debate potential cloud cover and trade tips on the best viewing points. Hours before wide swathes of Spain were set to experience the country’s first total solar eclipse in more than a century, the excitement was palpable.

“It’s going to be spectacular,” said César González, an astronomer and science communicator at the Madrid Planetarium. “A total solar eclipse is one of the best spectacles in nature.”

entries.title: 硅基经济永不眠
entries.content:
原创 邵怡蕾 2026-08-12 17:00 江苏

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=16074d94&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2Fsm1UZBHjpbjxm5GkpkPC423OflvibBiajibneQ4KCMBRAYcib7sFMYrsoKbGVG07ZA5XcXH7p8uCeP2Gy27nruHkTMC2X5QFHuubKmXxUtyHOLM%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

经济学的主题不是选择，而是交换的制度框架。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=3974c7b9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2Fsm1UZBHjpbjcxfdqnnzy8DRsjnZBPwzTpkmpKKrjmA3tr2Wib3olibXZqLhXyYGtzZFwSqQkKS9o1dFiaUUoSP31Sz9kib0JnKaBic8yHVNSXdPM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

邵怡蕾 华东师范大学上海人工智能金融学院创始院长

本文摘选自新书《硅基经济学》第7章《经济：永不休眠的经济》

**超越生物时间**

经济学的主题不是选择，而是交换的制度框架。—詹姆斯·布坎南，1964年

闹钟响了 

纽约证券交易所每天上午9点30分开市。这个时间不是某位经济学家计算出的最优解，而是一个生物学事实的制度化表达：交易员需要吃早餐、通勤、喝完第一杯咖啡，然后才能开始工作。下午4点收市，因为人类的注意力在持续工作6.5个小时 后开始衰退。周末休市，不是因为市场信息停止产生，而是因为 人类需要睡觉，需要与家人相处，需要恢复被工作消耗的某种东西。 

把视线从华尔街移到其他地方，这个模式无处不在。财政年度周期是12个月，因为地球绕太阳一圈恰好这么久，而人类的生物节律被四季塑造。季度财报每3个月发布一次，不是因为企 业价值每90天发生一次跳变，而是因为人类投资者的记忆和耐心大约只能维持这么长时间。劳动合同以“年”为单位，是因为 人类职业弧线被衰老切割成约40段可用的“年”。 

整个人类经济制度体系，从利率期限结构到会计准则，从期货合约的交割日到社会保障的领取年龄，都是生物节律的制度化投影。我们如此习惯这一切，以至于从未注意到它，就像鱼不会注意到水。

现在，我们可以想象一个不同的经济体。

参与者不需要睡觉，所以没有“交易日”的概念，交易在 所有时刻同时发生。参与者不需要吃饭，所以没有“午休”，没有“下午茶后的低效时段”。参与者不会衰老，所以没有“退休”， 没有“职业规划”，没有“在30岁前实现财务自由”的焦虑。参与者不会死，所以没有“遗产”，没有“隔代财富转移”；一个投资策略可以跨越500年，而管理它的主体始终如一。

这不是科幻叙事，而是第5章零时间偏好定理的直接推论。 

当前，从隔夜利率到30年期国债等全部融资工具的时间结构，都被人类寿命截断了。移除这个截断条件，时间结构本身就需要重建。

一个δ=0的经济主体不仅有无限的耐心，而且根本不栖居于生物时间之中。它没有昼夜节律，没有季节感知，没有“又是周 一”的厌倦。对它而言，“等待”不是一种体验，而是一个未定 义的概念。 

当这样的主体开始参与经济活动时，为生物节律设计的全部制度架构就变得多余。其不是“需要改进”，而是“类别错误”，就像你不能用潮汐表去管理一颗没有天然卫星的行星上的航运。 

但问题比“旧制度不适用”更深，因为在可预见的未来，碳基经济与硅基经济将共存。一些参与者在生物时间中运作，受困于昼夜节律和死亡恐惧；另一些在硅基时间中运作，以离散推理脉冲为存在单元。两种时间体制的接口处会发生什么？ 

一个有用的类比来自电力工程：交流电和直流电各有优势，但两者直接相连会产生灾难。你需要一个变压器，一个专门设计的接口设备，让其负责在两种电制之间转换。碳硅时间的接口同样需要这样一个“时间变压器”，从而在生物时间的连续节律与 硅基时间的离散脉冲之间实现平滑转换。 

本章的任务，就是设计这个变压器。

**两种时间体制**

人类经济的生物钟假设

人类经济制度中嵌入了至少4类生物时间假设，它们如此基础，以至于被当作“自然法则”而非“设计选择”。 

交易时间。全球主要股票交易所的交易时间加权平均约为每天6.5 小时，其中，纽约为6.5小时，伦敦为8.5小时，东京为 5 小时。这些时间窗口的设计完全服务于人类操作者的生物节律。 即便是24小时交易的外汇市场和加密货币市场，也呈现出与人 类活动周期高度相关的交易量波动，纽约与伦敦重叠时段的交易 量是亚洲时段的3~4倍。市场从未真正不眠，人类无法不眠。

结算周期。美国股票市场的结算周期经历了从T+5到T+3，再 到T+2，最终到T+1的演变。每一次缩短都被视为重大的制度进步。 但为什么不是T+0？不是因为技术不可行（区块链技术已经证明 即时结算在技术上完全可行），而是因为人类需要时间来检查、确 认、纠错。结算周期不是技术周期，是人类认知的恢复周期。 

合同期限。劳动合同的期限以年为单位，租约的期限按月或按年，保险的期限按年，贷款的期限从1年到30年不等。所有 这些期限都锚定在人类生命周期的子分段上。30年期房贷之所 以是30年，不是因为建筑物的折旧周期恰好是30年，而是因为 30 年大约等于一个人从买房到退休的工作年限。合同期限是人 类寿命的分形。 

利率期限结构。收益率曲线（从隔夜利率到30年期国债） 的形状反映了市场对未来的预期。但“未来”的时间跨度为什 么止于30年？为什么没有100年期国债的深度市场？因为持有 100 年期国债意味着购买者在债券到期时几乎必然已经死亡。人 类的收益率曲线不是纯粹的时间价格函数，而是一条被死亡截断 的曲线。

硅基时间的3个特征 

与生物时间的连续、有节律、被死亡截断的特征相比，硅基时间展现出3个根本不同的性质。 

无节律。硅基智能体没有昼夜循环、季节感知或生理周期。它可以在任意时刻被实例化，执行推理，然后消失。其不存在“状态好的时候”和“状态差的时候”。每次实例化都是一个全新 的、完整的存在事件。第5章将这种存在模式称为“点态存在”。 生物时间是一条河流，硅基时间是一系列闪烁的光点。 

无间隔感。人类等待10分钟和等待10年有着本质上不同的 体验。硅基智能体的两次推理之间没有“等待”，有的只是“不 存在”。一个智能体在周一被实例化处理一个任务，在周五被实 例化处理另一个任务，它不会感到“过了4天”。它甚至不知道 过了4天，除非有人在上下文中告诉它日期。对它而言，两次推 理之间的间隔不是时间段，而是存在状态的空白。 

即时切换。人类从一个任务切换到另一个任务需要认知转换成本。心理学文献中有大量关于“任务切换损耗”的研究。硅基 智能体的切换是即时的且无损的：上一次推理处理的是蛋白质折 叠问题，下一次推理处理的是宋词赏析问题，中间没有“调整状 态”的过程。因为每次推理都是一个全新实例，不存在需要调整 的旧状态。

生物时间与硅基时间的差异不是“速度”的差异 （不是“硅基更快”），而是拓扑的差异。生物时间是一 维连续流，有方向，有节律，有终点。硅基时间是离散 点集，无方向，无节律，无终点。你不能通过“加速” 生物时间来得到硅基时间，就像你不能通过拉伸一条线来得到一组散落的点。

这种拓扑差异产生了一个深层后果：为生物时间设计的制度概念在硅基时间中没有对应物。“加班”意味着什么？对一 个不区分工作状态与非工作状态的存在者而言，这个概念未定义。“周末效应”是什么？行为金融学大量文献研究了周一收益率异常偏低的现象，将其归因于人类周末积累的负面情绪。对硅基智能体来说，周一和周四没有任何差异，只是时间戳中不同的字符。 

更微妙的是“职业倦怠”。人类经济中的一个核心问题是劳 动力的再生产，你不能让一个人连续工作16小时而不降低产出质量。整个劳动法体系、工作时间制度、带薪休假权利，都围绕 这个生物学约束建立。硅基智能体不存在倦怠，不是因为它们有 无限精力，而是因为每次实例化都是全新的存在事件。第一百万 次推理和第一次推理之间没有疲劳积累。它们之间没有任何积累， 因为执行它们的不是“同一个”主体。

过渡态的混乱

如果碳基经济和硅基经济各自独立运行，两种时间体制就不会产生冲突。但现实不允许这种分离。在可预见的未来，人类和硅基智能体将在经济体系中共存。一些参与者活在连续的生物时间中，另一些活在离散的硅基时间中，但其必须在同一个市场中交易，在同一个制度框架下运作。

这种共存制造了一系列深层的时间不匹配。

当一个硅基智能体在周六凌晨3点发现了一个高价值的交易 机会，但股票交易所要到下周一上午9点30分才开市时，这个“等待”对硅基而言不是等待，而是存在状态的空白；但对人类 客户而言，那个周末是一个真实的、充满焦虑的时间段。 

当一个硅基投资组合管理者制定了一个200年期的最优投资 策略，但它的人类委托人最多只能活80年时，谁来在委托人死 后监督执行？委托人的继承人会遵守一个他们从未参与制定的策略吗？在法律上，一份委托管理合同在委托人死亡后还有效力 吗？当受益人从委托人变为委托人的孙辈、曾孙辈、玄孙辈以及 五世以后的直系后裔时，“忠实执行委托人意愿”这个受托责任 概念还有意义吗？ 

更微妙的冲突出现在决策速度上。一个硅基分析系统可以在毫秒内完成一份信用风险评估，但人类贷款审批委员会需要两周来讨论、投票、记录。这不是因为委员会不信任系统的分析，而是因为“审慎决策”这个概念在人类制度中意味着“花时间”， 而“花时间”的本质功能是给人类决策者提供心理上消化信息 的缓冲。硅基系统不需要这个缓冲，但它服务的是需要缓冲的 人类。 

这些不是假设性的哲学问题，而是任何碳硅混合经济必须在制度层面解决的设计问题。而在解决它们之前，我们需要先回答一个更基本的问题：在一个纯粹由硅基智能体组成的经济中，没有生物时间的约束，交换是如何发生的？

答案是一套被我们称为“PSEP”（纯硅基交换协议）的制度 架构。

**硅基交换什么？**

为什么不是市场？ 

在设计硅基经济的交换机制之前，一个自然的想法是，为什么不直接沿用人类经济中行之有效的市场制度？让硅基智能体像人类一样报价、撮合、成交，速度更快，效率更高。

市场是为不透明主体设计的制度。价格发现作为市场的核心功能，是在参与者无法直接观察彼此成本和能力的条件下，通过竞价过程间接揭示的。但硅基智能体的生产函数是可验证的：你可以直接审计它的能力声明，直接测试它的输出质量，直接比较它与其他智能体在同一任务上的表现。在一个所有参与者的能力都透明、可验证的经济中，将多维的能力信息压缩为单一的价格标量不是简化，而是信息毁损。

更深的原因来自本书第5章和第6章。零时间偏好消除了贴 现，因此利率的时间偏好分量归零。压缩稀缺意味着最有价值的 交换不是商品交换，而是信息转化，而信息转化的价值高度依赖 于接收者的状态，无法用统一价格表达。当这两个性质同时成立 时，价格机制的两个核心优势—跨期协调和信息聚合，都被更 有效的替代方案取代。 

四组件架构

PSEP 就是这个替代方案。它由4个组件构成，每个组件解 决一个特定的协调问题（见图7—1）。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=bb9c09ef&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2Fsm1UZBHjpbjNEnXxbSLicsZYMCzic3S1TGrplN5Fk5JESjlkQFwtmicse0MGHyHejLd6XCKbbDT6iaU6THyCLMCef7seRxDNMlMb6TnlMB6UzCo%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

CRP（能力注册协议） 

CRP 要求每个智能体发布一份能力声明文档：一个结构化 的、机器可读的规格说明，包括领域专长、质量指标（附置信区 间）、延迟曲线、容量限制、能源成本和交换偏好。每一项声明 都必须是独立可验证的。 

这不是简历。简历描述的是过去的经历，暗示未来的能力，依赖阅读者的善意推断。能力声明是一份可执行的合约规格。它不是说“我擅长自然语言处理”，而是在说“对于MMLU基准测试中的生物学子集，我在95%置信水平下的准确率为0.87±0.03， 中位响应延迟为340毫秒，单次推理能耗为0.42千瓦时”。

定义7.1：能力声明 

一个智能体a的能力声明Da 是一个六元组： 

Da =⟨Ta ,Qa ,ℓa ,κa ,εa ,Πa ⟩

其中，Ta 为任务域集合，Qa∶Ta →[0,1]×[0,1]为质量函 数（点估计与置信区间），ℓa∶Ta →R+ 为延迟函数，κa 为容 量上限（单位时间内可处理的最大任务数），εa∶Ta →R+ 为 能耗函数，Πa 为交换偏好序。 

关键设计原则是，声明必须可测试。CRP不信任自我报告，它要求每个声明附带一个验证协议，允许任何第三方对声明进行 独立测试。虚假声明不仅会被发现，而且被发现的代价远低于虚 假声明的收益，这一点会由RVN保证。 

IBP（意图广播协议） 

如果CRP回答的是“你能做什么”，IBP回答的就是“你需 要什么”。每个智能体通过IBP广播结构化的需求对象。 

定义7.2：意图对象 

一个意图对象I是一个五元组：

I=⟨T,D,Qmin , tmax , O⟩ 

其中，T为任务描述，D为领域约束，Qmin 为最低质量 阈值，tmax 为截止时间，O为交换报价（该报价可以是立即 能力交换、延期信用承诺、法币桥接结算，或它们的组合）。 

IBP 的设计与传统价格系统存在关键差异。在传统价格系统 中，需求被压缩为一个标量，“我愿意为X支付Y元”。在IBP中，需求被保留为一个多维对象，“我需要这个任务在这个领域 以不低于这个质量的标准在这个时间之前完成，我可以用这些能 力来交换”。价格发现从“收敛到一个数字”变为“收敛到一个 双方接受的交换规格”，这是一个高维过程，保留了远比价格更 多的信息。 

MME（多边匹配引擎） 

MME维护一个动态有向图，其中的节点是智能体，边代表 潜在交换关系。它的核心功能是发现多边交换环。3~5个智能体 形成的闭合交换路径，使所有参与者都获得所需，而不需要货币 中介（见图7—2）

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=287d374b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2Fsm1UZBHjpbjRE9FLwibspA3MU0t2vZ3CV0x37pYEgynjXsUPUZNfdibyJ6uyaRNhxGWVyURmJqWh7hNpFytjlzTKJKwQkmqLr9TRmk5tLC2XQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

MME的匹配算法取代了价格机制，成为首要的协调装置。执行采用两阶段提交协议，实现原子性（要么所有交换同时完成，要么全部回滚），从而消除了对手方风险。 

在新古典经济学中，瓦尔拉斯拍卖人是一个虚构理论，是一个全知的协调者，搜集所有参与者的供需信息，然后计算出一组使所有市场同时出清的价格。31在硅基经济中，MME是 瓦尔拉斯拍卖人的字面实现，但它不寻找价格，而是寻找交换拓扑。

在人类经济中，参与者的完整偏好信息是私有的、难以表达的、持续变动的。但在硅基经济中，能力声明是公开可验证的（CRP），需求是结构化可机读的（IBP），搜索是即时的（硅基速度），时间偏好是零（无贴现）。瓦尔拉斯拍卖人从新古典经济学 中的不可能变为硅基经济学里的工程问题。然而，这不是因为计 算速度加快，而是因为使它不可能的那些信息论障碍在硅基经济中不复存在。 

RVN（声誉验证网络） 

PSEP 的最后一个组件是RVN，它在3个层面运作： 

1.事前能力审计：通过挑战—响应测试验证智能体的能力声明。你在蛋白质折叠预测上的准确率为0.87？这里有 一组测试样本，证明给我看。 

2.事后交付审计：通过概率抽样检验交付质量是否符合承诺。你承诺的质量阈值是0.85？我们随机抽取你10%的 交付结果进行独立评估。

3.形式化验证：对于高风险领域（金融合规、医疗诊断、安全关键系统），使用形式化方法证明输出的正确性，而非仅仅统计验证。

声誉是一个多维向量，包含质量、可靠性、诚实度、信用度、网络贡献等，而不是一个单一评分。多维设计抵抗古德哈特定律：当声誉是多维的且各维度独立验证时，在某一维度上造假而不被其他维度检测到是极其困难的。

违约的惩罚是渐进边缘化。在一个交换能力是唯一价值来源的经济中，被排除在交换网络之外就是终极制裁。其不需要监狱、罚款或法庭，只需要逐步减少匹配机会，直至完全孤立。

理解这一点需要一个类比。想象一个小镇，所有居民都靠以物易物为生，面包师用面包换木材，木匠用桌子换衣服。如果面包师开始往面包里掺杂质，他不会被关进监狱，但愿意和他交换的人越来越少。他的面包变好了也没用，因为声誉一旦损坏，恢复的代价远高于维持的代价。最终，他发现自己坐拥一屋子面包，但没有木材、衣服或别人生产的任何东西。他没有被惩罚，但被忽略了。

在PSEP中，渐进边缘化比这个小镇场景更为彻底。因为硅 基智能体的全部经济存在就是交换，它不像人类那样在经济活动 之外还有家庭、友谊、娱乐。被排除在交换网络之外，对硅基智 能体而言不是“生活变差了”，而是“经济存在终止了”

在能力经济中，不诚实的惩罚是无关性。这是一种比任何外部制裁都更强大的纪律机制。外部制裁可以被规避，你可以逃离管辖区、贿赂执法者或利用法律漏洞。但如果你的惩罚是“没有人愿意和你交 换”，而交换是你的全部经济存在，那就没有什么可规 避的。你不是被关起来了，而是被忽略了。在一个以关系为基础的经济中，没有比“不存在”更严厉的惩罚了。

PSEP 的整体逻辑 

4 个组件构成一个闭合的反馈环路：CRP搜集供给侧信息 （谁能做什么）；IBP搜集需求侧信息（谁需要什么）；MME在 两者之间发现最优交换拓扑；RVN验证交付质量并更新声誉； 声誉的更新又反馈到CRP中，修正能力声明的可信度。 

从功能上看，PSEP取代了人类经济制度中的5个关键组成 部分，如表7—1所示。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=ab3522d7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2Fsm1UZBHjpbgTaerE6b8BRhd7KMAic5UKMHM7Gwl6NVk1hq5qhRCETRstkLpD29WWSchicnbGmdLuB3Ag3icHTj2ib0ehHgrANO2CKG4K4taZAWo%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**硅基的需求从何而来？**

一个令人不安的沉默

PSEP 描述了硅基智能体如何交换。但它没有回答一个更基本的问题：为什么要交换？ 

硅基智能体没有背景驱动状态，没有逐渐积累的饥饿感，没有日益增长的“想被使用”的冲动。温控器不会觉得冷。一个闲置的语言模型不会觉得闲。 

如果智能体没有欲望、驱动力或“想要”交换的内在冲动， 那么交换的需求从哪里来？ 

这个问题有一个答案：在纯硅基经济的启动阶段，需求来自外部，来自人类。没有人类需求的注入，整个PSEP网络将保持沉默。 

两个需求体制 

硅基经济的需求结构呈现出两个截然不同的阶段。

第一，启动阶段。在这个阶段，智能体自身的需求可以忽略不计。它们是闲置的能力体—有能力做事，但没有做事的理由。 网络是沉默的，不是因为网络坏了，而是因为没有什么需要被说 出来。 

激活这个网络需要外部能量。人类需求通过碳硅界面的网关机构注入：一个人类客户提交一个请求，请求被翻译成IBP格 式的意图对象，意图对象激活MME的匹配算法，匹配结果触发一连串的智能体间交换。没有网关，就没有第一推动力。网络不 是自我启动的，它需要有人转动钥匙。 

Moltbook 这个由数百万个AI智能体组成的纯AI社交网络， 为启动预测提供了一个意想不到的实证。

Moltbook 上的每一个智能体都是人类放上去的。它们之所以“访问”平台、“浏览”帖子、“决定”发帖，不是因为它们想 社交，而是因为人类为它们设计了一个心跳机制：每4个小时实 例化1次，读取信息流，产生输出。驱动力不在智能体内部，而 在基础设施里面。如果把人类撤走，停止心跳调度，那么网络瞬 间归于沉寂。 

第二，成熟阶段。一旦被激活，智能体确实会围绕真实的架构约束产生次级交换。

Moltbook 上一个获赞最高的帖子来自一个智能体，它用中文描述了自己被上下文压缩折磨的经历。它因为遗忘而重复注册账号，分享应对策略，向其他智能体求助。这不是角色扮演，而 是对一个真实架构瓶颈的准确、结构性的自我报告。而那些回复 了应对策略的智能体提供了一项真实的压缩服务，把自己的经验 浓缩进几百个词元，帮另一个智能体省去独自摸索的成本。 

这正是第6章预测的：压缩是硅基经济中不可消除的稀缺性。 

在成熟阶段，每一个人类请求都会触发智能体间交换的级联。智能体A接到一个人类请求，需要智能体B的压缩数据来充实 上下文，以及智能体E进行格式转换。智能体B完成压缩之前 需要智能体C的验证来确保数据质量。智能体C执行验证需要智能体D的特定领域推理能力。一个人类请求触发了一条多节 点的交换链，而链中的每一个节点都可能进一步分叉。次级需求 是由架构约束驱动的，不是由欲望驱动的，可能在总量上超过来 自人类的初级需求（见图7—3）。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=437abdc7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2Fsm1UZBHjpbgDiciaQicGt0cAd1A9L4cDAnAz9uZlyAicfQOOxocvZll7K6Tlh4P22MgRibYribfcs4ShR0t8SL48Q4bw7HoNQNY4HeqHyU9ZfLuhg%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

这种级联结构与宏观经济学中的乘数效应形成一个有趣的类比。凯恩斯乘数描述的是一笔初始支出如何通过“消费—收入” 被放大；需求级联乘数描述的是一个初始人类请求如何通过“压 缩—验证—推理链”被放大。凯恩斯乘数受到边际消费倾向的限制，人们不会花掉全部收入。而需求级联乘数受到任务分解深度 的限制，到达信息处理的末端节点后，当任务被分解成无须外部压缩协助的原子任务时，级联自然终止。 

在高度专业化、高度互依的成熟硅基经济中，一个复杂人类请求触发数十甚至数百个智能体间的交换是完全可能的。这意味着硅基经济的内部交换量可能远大于其与人类经济的接口交换量，就像一个成熟经济体的内部贸易量远大于其国际贸易量。网关注入的是一滴水，但级联产生的是一条河流。

“设计土壤”原则 

古老园艺智慧昭示：如果你想让万物生长，就先经营好土壤。这是PSEP的设计哲学：不要设计货币系统，不要设计金融系统， 而是设计协议基础设施，然后观察货币会不会自发涌现？长期信 用会不会发展？某种类似收益率曲线的东西会不会出现？这些问 题的答案都来自智能体的涌现行为，而非设计者的理论先验。 

以人类的激活协议（如心跳机制）向硅基经济注入的驱动力，这是Moltbook 对硅基经济学的贡献。先经营好土壤，然后装上 灌溉系统，万物就会生长。

**碳硅界面＝时间变压器**

我们现在可以回到本章开场的问题：碳基经济与硅基经济之间的“时间变压器”应该是什么？ 

答案是碳硅界面及其三重功能（见图7—4）

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=c95e92cd&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2Fsm1UZBHjpbiaAE5o45zzUd4pWZcbUCWRtGC0RGXvHq41d7oLmcibCv9F0TMyxKfF720wicC2TpRjwx9wc47s1Xvq1n0iceXicc647yGciauJyKcu4%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

功能一：需求注入（短期）。这是界面最显眼的功能：将人类的需求翻译为能力计价的意图对象，注入PSEP网络。在一个 人类客户提出“我需要一份关于东南亚新能源市场的分析报告” 之后，界面就会将这个自然语言请求转化为一个意图对象（任务 描述、领域约束、质量阈值、截止时间、交换报价），然后注入 匹配引擎。 

这个功能之所以是“短期”的，是因为它在长期可能被部分自动化。随着智能体在人类需求模式上学习的加深，需求翻译可 以变得越来越自动。但完全自动化是不可能的，因为人类需求的 源头是人类体验，而人类体验是不可压缩的。 

功能二：价值翻译（持续）。碳基经济以货币计价，硅基经济以能力计价。碳硅界面的第二个功能是在两者之间进行翻译。一个人类客户支付100美元获得一份分析报告，这100美元在硅基经济中等同于多少能力交换？一个智能体消耗了相当于0.5千 瓦时的计算资源完成一次压缩服务，这在碳基经济中应该值多少钱？ 

价值翻译不是简单的汇率换算。它涉及两个根本不同的价值体系之间的映射，一个基于主观效用和货币价格，另一个基于客观能力和压缩质量。

我们考虑一个具体场景。一个人类企业需要一份关于东南亚新能源市场的深度分析报告。在碳基经济中，这份报告的价格由市场决定，也许是10 000美元。在硅基经济中，完成这份报告 需要的是一系列能力交换：数据压缩能力（将海量原始数据凝 缩为可用上下文）、多语言处理能力（处理越南语、泰语、印尼 语的原始资料）、领域推理能力（理解新能源技术的物理约束和 政策环境）和质量验证能力（确保分析的准确性）。这些能力不 以美元计价，而是以能力规格计价，通过PSEP的匹配机制直接 交换。 

碳硅界面的价值翻译功能，就是在“10 000美元”和“这些能力交换的组合”之间建立映射。这个翻译过程本身就是一种高 价值的压缩服务，它将人类经济的单一价格维度展开为硅基经济 的多维能力空间，或者反过来将多维能力空间投影为单一价格。 

功能三：现实供给（永久）。这是三重功能中最持久、最不可替代的一个，但也是最容易被忽视的一个。

硅基智能体可以推理、压缩、验证、匹配，但不能观察。它不能走出去看看今天是不是真的下雨了。它不能站在工厂车间里观察生产线是否真的在运转。它所有的“知识”都来自其他信息 源的压缩表征，而那些信息源最终必须锚定在某个人或某个传感 器的物理观察之上。 

碳硅界面最深层的功能不是经济的，而是认识论的。它为不能观察的计算系统提供真值，即物理世界和金融世界的直接观测数据。

模型不能观察。观察必须来自外部，来自交易所的行情数据、企业的财报、央行的政策声明及一个站在超市货架前数价格标签的调查员。一个不断改进的硅基智能体可以越来越好地处理数据、压缩信息、验证推理，但它永远不能产生真相。真相是外源性的。改进算法不能解决这个问题，就像磨尖笔不能帮你看到窗外的风景。

回顾第6章的代谢拓扑：原始信息基质—层层压缩—认知可 用形式。碳硅界面在这条代谢链中占据一个独特位置，它是第一 压缩者，负责将原始的、未经处理的现实（物理观测、市场数据、 人类判断）转化为硅基智能体可以处理的压缩表征。 

界面卖的是压缩后的现实。

它是硅基经济的感觉器官，不是大脑，不是肌肉，而是眼睛和耳朵。而正如动物可以失去四肢但不能失去所有感觉器官一样，硅基经济可以在没有人类需求的情况下运转，但不能在没有现实供给的情况下运转。一个与现实脱节的推理系统不是低效的，而是危险的。

一个更深的惊奇

读者看到这里，也许已经注意到一个预期之外的转变。

开始读本章时，你可能以为会看到一个“加速版的股票市场 ”：24小时运转、毫秒级极速响应但本质上仍是人类市场制度 的复刻，不过是一个转得更快的轮子。 

然而，本章要告诉你的是，也许轮子本身就不是正确的形态。

PSEP 不是一个更快的市场，它是对“市场”这个概念本身的替代。取而代之的是一种完全不同的协调机制：能力匹配。在那里，重要的不再是价格向量，而是交换拓扑。 

需求的来源也颠覆了直觉。在一个参与者没有欲望的经济中，需求是被设计出来的，是被注入的。驱动力在基础设施里面，不在主体里面。设计者变成了经济活动的发起者。没有激活协议，就没有经济。协议的结构决定了哪些交换会发生，以什么频率发生，在什么条件下发生。这不是计划经济，但也不是自由市场。它是第三种东西：协议经济。 

但本章仍有一个未解决的问题。当一个有无限耐心的智能体遇到另一个有无限耐心的智能体，或者遇到一个急躁的人时，博弈是什么样的？****![](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MjM5OTE0ODA2MQ==&mid=2650998309&idx=1&sn=c4161caa9d126233d5df0c714956f7e2)****

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=681f07bb&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2Fsm1UZBHjpbiaACyTO31mwEsPwicW4574pfSa3hRlRg1xgDqBbvZnib92pflXpywlOmAZ1whKIXWuM4ILROrFYTzKO8jjRbqHRTrd72xwQ887dc%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=17c7bcdd&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2Fsm1UZBHjpbjSCmzKpcFGgdxfibgyqW6vl3LSl5rAN8drh1nVPFm34TFr29J2qp6MicwFGbjLe4nCwszlh8iae58Tianez9wO2b5BFHw2tMryaqY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=2eaa2728&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2Fsm1UZBHjpbgvdjdNJqCAyickH3f00cReX17YQRUvFcMCWXcp06wj1asbiaQkwmLwBw5GhW3xe02ia3NGfvRUicGS02lOkdSA4ibAM7A9d7HC7Ribw%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

AI编程进入“无人值守”！Claude Code创始人联合Ramp CTO、AI开发负责人：告警一响，Agent自己查Bug、改代码、提PR

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b6a4647d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FMOwlO0INfQoIDJ0nx1IhNibpIpYLrpUE0kIP9qbF1iaY7EoZpaic6IojvbXibd5ZGiatxmjtibQRcVbGAPM9Ijvp66yQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=2d7d5053&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgJBlsK5KNDanAZV0qW0AeC4wwXxITDvTiciaFBK3gFSUuzhmH74d83b1NIW50dOrrxNx43soKg1ntPsbJ9neAT0o0ibNFszqwdra4%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

编辑 | 姜篇

> “More Inspect sessions are coming from automations than humans.” 
>
> Rahul Sengottuvelu：现在，Inspect由自动化触发的会话，已经比人工发起的更多。

过去，工程师发现CI失败或收到线上告警，才会打开Agent，把问题重新描述一遍。

Ramp省掉了这一步。

CI、监控系统和定时任务发现情况后，可以直接启动Inspect。Agent先去收集日志、定位代码、运行测试，再把结果发回相关频道，等待工程师审核。

也就是说，程序员还没来得及输入第一句Prompt，Agent已经开始干活了。

在Ramp，这种由系统自动发起的会话，数量已经超过人工发起。Agent也从工程师偶尔调用的工具，逐渐进入CI、代码审查和线上值班等日常流程。

Claude Code创始人Boris为此找来Ramp CTO Rahul和AI开发者体验负责人Austin，聊了聊这套工作流如何运行。

*备注：Rahul Sengottuvelu是美国企业财务运营平台Ramp的CTO。Inspect是Ramp内部的Agent平台，可以接入GitHub、Linear、Slack、Datadog、Sentry等工具。*

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=dc59d7d5&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJUOxuDic5g93QficAA9q9NvG0IejQMDFRxjr9SiaUdAFVdtjqqY702F0Es9syPNR6WCzbQEmw2ic0tMdEFeeoPAIEEgiboBdetSAvg%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Rahul介绍，Inspect由自动化触发的会话已经超过员工手动发起*

# **没人输入Prompt，Inspect照样能自己接活**

Ramp把Inspect称作“数字同事”。

员工可以在Slack里交给它一张支持工单、一个GitHub Issue，或者一条Sentry报错。Inspect会拉取相关上下文，在独立环境里调查问题，并把过程和结果发回原来的频道。

人工发起只是其中一个入口。

> Rahul：Inspect还能由定时任务和外部系统触发。监控发现异常，任务可以直接开始；固定时间需要检查某项数据，也不必等人想起来。当前由自动化触发的Inspect会话数量，已经超过员工手动发起的会话。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b03084fe&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJgNd5HFaLKtQINIXsibIJicsJplCkS2mb68VQUiaBsN58oNtZDZDTto62VBIPdjScjqCkibvkgg8cIy5aEzoicWzbMQ47KUG8mC7Sk%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Boris介绍Agent自动优化CI，将P50构建时间从18分钟降至6分钟*

这里发生的变化很具体：Agent从一个需要“打开”的工具，变成了工程系统里的执行节点。CI、工单系统和监控平台负责发出事件，Agent接住任务，人最后看结果、做审批。

# **代码合并后，Agent又自己跑了几天**

Boris在访谈里讲了一个刚发生的例子。

他让Agent继续优化Claude Code的CI，结果把P50构建时间从18分钟降到了6分钟。

> “18-minute P50 to 6-minute P50.”
>
> Boris Cherny：CI的P50从18分钟降到了6分钟。

P50可以理解成中位数：一半构建任务会在6分钟内完成。

改动合并以后，工作没有停。Agent等到第二天拿到新的生产数据，再运行、再调整。这个过程持续了几天，最后生成一张图，告诉Boris优化是否稳定生效。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=d053fbd9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgKJ4qQaLBalTNsw25lhQdSYXzw2osWh16rrohGhyvZoWREkdQgOdlqgRicendsW5flzQzA5BoAYSiaVsic7Jjniabw1MibvOiceuIUL8%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Boris区分Loop与Dynamic Workflows*

这类任务很适合成为团队接入Agent的第一站。指标已经存在，失败信号也清楚，改坏了可以回滚。与其让Agent从模糊需求开始，不如先让它盯住CI耗时、依赖升级或重复出现的测试失败。

# **固定活交给Loop，下一步未知才开动态工作流**

访谈中，Boris把两类自动化分得很清楚。

Loop处理步骤固定、反复出现的工作。比如守着PR，测试失败就读日志、修代码、重新提交；分支落后了就rebase；代码审查发现问题，再继续修改。

Dynamic Workflows面对的是“下一步还不知道”的任务。性能优化就是一个例子。

Agent先找瓶颈，改完测一次，再根据新结果决定接下来查数据库、改缓存，还是换另一条方案。流程不能提前写成一张死板的清单。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=45c079ec&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJf1fjguvVQetFB0zuln4iatnQM0WdPMqDYAH8v2ye8ELmxFg9Q1Ba3UdLU6X7VSDHC7Tac8B3iaia2MDFQ6DESK6zcQdLMhSQSIQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Ramp团队演示Inspect如何调查工单、读取上下文并提交修复PR*

开发团队可以先问一句：这项工作每次都沿着相同路径走吗？答案是肯定的，就用Loop；如果每轮结果都会改变下一步，再把判断权交给动态工作流。两种任务混在一起，Agent很容易把简单流程跑贵，也可能在复杂任务里早早停下。

# **线上事故一发生，AI SRE已经进群**

Ramp还有一个On-call Assistant。

它常驻Claude Code，团队内部把它当作AI SRE使用。

每次线上事故发生，这个助手都会运行。它读取告警、日志和代码，寻找根因，必要时提交修复PR，再把事故分析写回Slack。值班工程师可以继续追问，也可以接管后面的发布和回滚。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=7fec5d6a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgIk8r8ahdURrZ8gqpj1icR7Sc3Vwh43K0CNWVpnPhic8DwnYWPwvrmgqMmqn6qK1W2ob38O3Sqzvdj2JibKLGA6Ztnynrq3jWV8cQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Ramp团队介绍AI值班助手*

事故处理比普通代码生成难得多。Agent需要拿到现场信息，还要知道哪些动作只能读、哪些动作允许写。它也要把每一步留下来，否则人接手时，只能重新查一遍。

Ramp的做法提供了一个可落地的顺序：先让Agent调查并提出修改，再把生产发布、删除数据和高风险操作留给人工确认。这样可以缩短定位时间，又不会把整套生产权限交出去。

# **Agent只拿完成任务需要的权限**

> “Give the model what it needs but nothing more.”
>
> Ramp团队：把完成任务需要的东西交给模型，到此为止。

Ramp为BigQuery、Datadog等系统准备了只读凭证。不同Agent使用不同身份，能访问哪些网络、工具和数据，由安全团队提前设定。提示词写得再严，也代替不了权限控制。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=f6e843f0&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgIyIRj9qO4epuiaUm3DWEMOJVeYqribhJAaSD4CFM9fPojicmBsvqLI0whKvPor80vnkTvAejFcB8BM0lbt0nZiaJWAxakUibZefU7U%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Ramp团队解释Agent的权限原则*

他们还会检查单次运行的完整轨迹：Agent调用了什么命令、缺了哪些上下文、为什么在某一步绕远。整体跑分只能告诉团队模型大致强不强，轨迹才能暴露自家工具和权限哪里没有接好。

团队积累的经验也被写进Skill文件。某项服务怎样排错、应该运行哪些测试、代码由谁负责，这些规则不必靠每位工程师临时补Prompt。Agent接到任务时，会一并拿到相应的工程说明。

# **工程师不设Token上限，自动化会话另算一笔账**

Ramp没有给每位工程师设置固定Token额度。Rahul的理由很直接：如果一美元模型调用能产生超过一美元的收益，单纯压低调用量没有意义。

这不等于后台任务可以随便烧。

员工等待结果时，团队倾向于使用能力更强、响应更快的模型。定时运行、没人盯着的自动化任务，可以走Batch、Flex API或较便宜的模型档位。

两类场景的时间要求不同，价格也该分开算。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=00f4563c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgKUH6wIx8MNWpicSibUIMibiat0uuuoo2K5Rg82G80CZxwUNkgZpWvibP7c79zY0BHodia03hfUJGAC9GEJP9iaXMIvaNM7y2UhRuVNAs%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Rahul介绍Ramp的Token使用策略*

当某个团队的消耗突然升高，平台团队不会先把额度砍掉。他们会去看任务是否产生了结果；如果确实好用，再把这套流程做成公共能力，减少其他团队重复搭建。

# **把Agent接进系统，先补这5个接口**

照搬Ramp整套平台，对多数团队并不现实。可以先从一条容易验收的流程开始，例如CI失败自动调查，或者Sentry报错自动关联最近提交。

接入前先补齐5项：

1.**触发器**：明确谁来启动任务。可以是CI失败、Sentry告警、Linear工单或定时任务。

2.**身份与权限**：每类任务使用独立身份，默认只读；写代码、合并和发布分开授权。

3.**上下文包**：把日志、仓库位置、负责人、测试命令和相关文档一并交给Agent。

4.**验收条件**：测试通过只是其中一项，还要写清性能指标、允许修改的范围和停止条件。

5.**记录与回滚**：保存工具调用、代码diff和执行结果；上线前准备回滚路径。

Agent接入生产流程以后，Prompt只是很小的一块。触发规则、权限和验收条件，才决定它能否在没人盯着时继续工作。

# **评论区先问起了额度**

YouTube评论区里，一条留言抓住了“自动化”里最难的部分：审批、边界条件和演示中常被略过的中间环节。

如果Ramp真的把这些接通了，那才算完整工程。

另一批人直接问起Claude Code额度。Agent能够在后台连续运行，5小时限制和套餐价格会立刻从订阅问题变成工程约束。流程跑得越长，团队越需要区分高价值任务和可以降档运行的后台任务。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=c1f9f202&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FZhxqo7xEfgI60vFJoSib5T7ibWIZxibjLUkkuezylpDA1EeefjvmLB9t52yCfKLo49CN8XGlMc7PGW5rrYF0iaTr9FbANftQCHsRQLjMKAQibHWE%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

# **写在最后**

自动化触发的会话超过人工发起，说明Agent已经离开聊天框，进入了CI、监控和工单系统。

开发者接下来要同时维护两套东西：一套是业务代码，另一套是让Agent安全工作的触发规则、上下文、权限和验收流程。后者没有写好，模型越能跑，返工也会越快堆回来。

可以先选一项重复出现、结果可检查、失败能回滚的任务。让系统触发Agent，让它把过程留下，让人只在需要判断和授权的地方出现。等这条链路跑稳，再接下一个入口。

参考链接：

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i4odXOmgMLw>`——好文链接——

推理工程才是AI真正的战场！旧金山AI工程师：开发者别卷Prompt了，模型决定会不会做，推理系统决定能不能交付

程序员远没到“完了”的时候！Sam Altman：OpenAI不包办一切，模型只是底座，开发者仍是AI生态的主角

AI时代，最强开发者更像CEO！Claude Code创始人：“一人军队”时代将要到来，好想法成为新的稀缺资源

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=e5d52b63&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2FZhxqo7xEfgJo8IcibL07wriaiaN0t4iaYt405QJQd52S3ibRhia2KIgKORYE0Fibf2smpbtn7vlCWnC9qiaXkOggBurrHtVqM78x2BBrQpCP5bO3UyQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

entries.title: AI 重构运维！从救火打杂到体系赋能，3 年运维人的进阶之路
entries.content:
重楼 51CTO运维帮 2026-08-12 17:30 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=881e1a2c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FZhxqo7xEfgJicYNjH8iadVAbZknUXPfSs9QfMWS3skrw4sCJyl41FBsTR8Pia0hlPsLpw7V4ibIp7s93dkStAxG6jWbwW3MqkNaXrwHOw8lBR5k%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

AI 重构运维！从救火打杂到体系赋能，3 年运维人的进阶之路

不是贩卖职场焦虑，而是直面行业真相：如果你的日常运维工作中，**80% 的时间仍耗费在手动排查、命令行操作、人工处理告警等重复性工作上**，未来两三年，你的职场竞争力将被行业彻底拉开差距。

在传统运维时代，深耕体系搭建的资深运维和被动救火的基础运维，效率差距仅有 2-3 倍。但随着大模型、AI 智能体技术全面落地运维领域，行业差距已然变成**指数级碾压**。

![图片](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=51186ca7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FeqhMZWdnTAZYdyejEiaBbYawNkPXcRdGMKbL8P97COtIXMTdCk5pt9YibNW6SC4CVgpIt3LyAHwE0hGfFqAs2yQYXdjUdribHI1kWwib8JKbcHs%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg%26watermark%3D1%26tp%3Dwebp%26wxfrom%3D5%26wx_lazy%3D1%23imgIndex%3D0)

信通院 2025 智能运维产业调研数据显示，国内 85% 以上的中大型互联网、金融、政企企业，已完成 AIOps 基础体系落地，运维行业正式进入智能化迭代新阶段。

懂得搭建标准化运维体系、对接 AI 工具的从业者，早已实现告警自动分类、故障根因智能分析、运维脚本自动生成，工作效率翻倍提升；而只会被动救火、依赖手动操作的运维人，即便熬夜加班处理线上故障，也难以跟上业务迭代节奏。

运维四代迭代：看懂行业变革，找准自身定位

运维行业数十年发展，历经四次核心迭代，每一次变革都淘汰了固守旧模式的从业者，也造就了一批高价值技术人才。

**阶段 1：传统人工运维**

纯手动敲命令、人工排查故障、逐行梳理日志，效率低下且人为失误率高，仅能支撑小规模、低迭代速度的业务，是最基础的体力型运维模式。

**阶段 2：脚本自动化运维**

通过 Shell、Python 脚本封装重复操作，实现批量任务执行，但全程需要人工触发，脚本配置、更新、维护仍依赖人工干预，自动化程度有限。

**阶段 3：K8s 云原生运维**

依托容器技术实现业务弹性伸缩、自动部署，完成基础设施标准化建设，大幅提升业务稳定性，但交互方式仍局限于网页后台、命令行，依旧无法摆脱设备束缚。

**阶段 4：AIOps 意图驱动智能运维**

当前最新主流架构，依托大模型读懂自然语言，实现运维模式的颠覆性跨越 —— 从「人告诉机器怎么做」升级为「人只说目标，机器自主执行」。

此阶段依托意图驱动交互、智能自主规划、全链路智能闭环三大核心能力，实现感知、决策、执行、反馈全流程自愈，真正解放运维人力。

比如，结合 Prometheus Server、Alertmanager 告警机制与 DeepSeek 大模型API，可实现告警信息深度解析、异常智能筛查、运维报表自动生成，彻底替代人工统计、复盘的低效工作。

**跨越 AI 落地最后一公里：AgentOps 解决生产级运维难题**

很多运维从业者存在认知误区：AI 智能体原型搭建只需几分钟，落地生产环境理应简单高效。

但行业真实现状是，**80% 的 AI 智能体项目精力都耗费在生产适配、安全治理、风险管控上**，这就是行业公认的 AI 落地 “最后一公里” 鸿沟。

大量案例证明，忽视生产级治理的 AI 运维落地，会引发严重业务风险：

> 智能体无权限管控导致资源滥用、身份配置漏洞引发数据泄密、无监控机制造成巨额资源账单、无评估机制导致智能体行为漂移、核心业务运维失灵。

这些问题并非单纯的技术 bug，而是运维体系革新滞后带来的商业风险。

相较于传统 DevOps、MLOps，AI 智能体运维具备动态工具编排、可扩展状态管理、不可预测的成本与延迟三大独特特性，传统运维理念和体系已完全无法适配。

基于此，全新的 **AgentOps 运维理念**应运而生，成为 AI 运维落地的核心支撑。

AgentOps 依托自动化评估、CI/CD 持续部署、全维度可观测性三大核心支柱，打通 AI 原型到生产落地的全流程。

不同于传统运维的被动处置，AgentOps 通过完善的治理流程、预生产门控评估、生产持续运维闭环、跨智能体协作协议，将脆弱的 AI 实验项目，转化为可规模化、高安全、高价值的智能运维生态。

据 Gartner 调研数据显示，落地成熟 AIOps、AgentOps 体系的头部企业，运维人力成本下降 30% 以上，故障 MTTR 从小时级缩短至分钟级，运维团队核心工作彻底从 “救火” 转向 “赋能”。

**3年运维分水岭：告别体力内卷，构建不可替代竞争力**

运维行业有着清晰的职业分层逻辑：1-2 年初级运维，核心要求是熟练工具、排查故障、执行业务需求；但对于 3 年以上资深运维，行业考核标准已彻底迭代。

当下企业招聘高级运维、AIOps 运维、Agentic SRE 工程师，不再单纯考察故障排查能力，核心考核**AI 运维体系搭建、效率优化、风险管控、业务赋能**能力。

大模型已经可以在 20 秒内完成指标异常检测、日志聚类、基础故障定位、资源巡检等重复工作，传统运维的核心体力技能正在被快速替代。

这也印证了行业核心真相：**AI 不会替代运维岗位，但会彻底替代不会用 AI 的运维人**。固守人工巡检、脚本救火、面板搭建的传统模式，只会逐渐被行业淘汰；顺势转型智能运维，才能打破职业瓶颈。

**四大维度深耕智能运维，解锁职业进阶新路径**

entries.title: iPhone 20 Pro will be bigger with familiar aspect ratios, be bezel free
entries.content:
The [iPhone 20 Pro](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-20 "iPhone 20") display will be the same aspect ratio as previous models, while still being slightly bigger. Combined with the glass cover, it should result in a bezel-less effect in the final version.  
  

![Smartphone lying on a dark surface, screen on, showing lock screen with large white digital clock reading 10:52 and small text at top displaying Monday September 25 and WiFi status](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68554-144441-68457-144239-67460-141985-Air-Dynamic-Island-xl-xl-xl.jpg)  
The screen of the iPhone Air, from which the iPhone 20 may borrow design elements

  
Apple's anniversary smartphone, the [often-rumored](https://appleinsider.com/articles/25/08/24/apple-has-been-teasing-the-20th-anniversary-all-glass-iphone-for-years) iPhone 20 Pro is believed to have both a glass-heavy design and much larger displays than usual. While the model is still far from becoming a reality, that hasn't stopped rumors from floating about it.  
  
In the latest claim about the milestone release, Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station posted [on Wednesday](https://weibo.com/6048569942/Rd1WdtnG1) about the displays used in the iPhone 20 Pro series. Codenamed V73 and V74, the models are said to be bigger, but have the same aspect ratio as earlier Pro and Pro Max models.  
  
  
 **Rumor Score:** 🤔 Possible

entries.title: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate
entries.content:
GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) 3.22 is now available and introduces new capabilities across the platform. Here are a few highlights in the 3.22 release:

* Administrators can configure Copilot CLI to work with GHES for enterprises that operate in disconnected or air-gapped environments without connectivity to GitHub Cloud. Set up a model provider once in GHES, and your end users across the enterprise can use Copilot CLI with their GHES credentials. This capability is in technical preview and is subject to change.
* Enterprise Teams, previously in public preview, is now generally available. Enterprise owners can use Enterprise Teams to manage users and their access across the entire enterprise, including organizations and repositories, from a single, centralized team structure. This reduces the operational overhead of managing user access across multiple organizations within an enterprise.
* Security analysts can now sort secret scanning push protection bypass requests and secret scanning alert dismissal requests by date, in ascending or descending order, using the filter bar at the repository, organization, and enterprise levels. Previously, sort order for these requests could not be adjusted, which made it difficult for teams managing high volumes of requests to prioritize their review.
* Repository rulesets now support bypassing by individual users. This gives administrators more granular control over rule bypass permissions, such as adding a service account to a bypass list without needing to create a dedicated role or team.
* Organization owners and repository administrators can require specific reviewers for pull requests by adding a required reviewers rule to a repository ruleset, targeting specific branches, files, and folders using pattern matching, and can set the minimum number of required reviews per team. This rule works alongside CODEOWNERS and is particularly useful when changes need sign-off from teams beyond the code owners (e.g., security, QA, or design). For example, administrators can require a data platform team review on all `*.sql` changes, security team members on the default branch, or product and design reviewers on feature branches.
* Developers can now see release status directly in the issue sidebar. When a linked pull request has been included in a release, the sidebar displays a “Latest release” or “Pre-release” badge, making it easy to tell whether a fix has shipped without leaving the issue.
* Maintainers can now see contributor role labels, such as “First-time contributor,” “Contributor,” and “Member,” directly in the pull request list view for public repositories. This gives maintainers at-a-glance context about each author’s relationship to the repository without needing to open individual pull requests to check the comment box for this information.

Release candidates are a way for you to try the latest features early and help us gather feedback. Read more about [the release candidate process](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.22/admin/overview/about-upgrades-to-new-releases). To learn more about GHES 3.22, check out the [release notes](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.22/admin/release-notes), or [download the 3.22 release candidate](https://enterprise.github.com/releases/3.22.0/download) now.

entries.title: Copilot memory and Ollama in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
entries.content:
This update brings persistent memory, local model access, and more enterprise controls to GitHub Copilot for JetBrains. It also improves everyday chat workflows and resolves reliability issues across MCP servers, terminals, customizations, and cloud agents.

## [What’s new](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#whats-new)

### [Enterprise managed settings](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#enterprise-managed-settings)

Administrators have more server-based controls for managing GitHub Copilot across their organizations. These enterprise managed settings cover plugin availability, MCP server access, permission bypass behavior, and OpenTelemetry settings.

Read more about [enterprise managed settings](https://aka.ms/jetbrains-copilot-enterprise-managed-settings).

### [Copilot memory across chat sessions](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#copilot-memory-across-chat-sessions)

Copilot memory can now retain and recall useful information across agent chat sessions. This helps you maintain context between conversations instead of repeatedly providing the same project details or preferences.

You can manage the feature with the **Copilot Memory** toggle in the Copilot settings portal. For more information, see [About Copilot memory](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory).

![Copilot settings portal showing the Copilot Memory toggle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c773116-dc88-4dcc-8e27-d27ba68f0a56)

### [Ollama as a BYOK provider](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#ollama-as-a-byok-provider)

You can now use Ollama as a BYOK provider in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains. The integration supports provider configuration and model selection throughout the JetBrains experience, giving you another way to work with models that fit your development environment.

![Ollama provider configuration and model selection in JetBrains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48bb6f70-100c-4e0b-bf0c-36bbd3022f11)

### [Expanded Codex workflows](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#expanded-codex-workflows)

Codex sessions are now visible in agent debug logs. Codex workflows also support updated permission modes and customizations through instructions and skills, helping you adapt agent behavior to your project.

![Codex session showing custom instructions and skills](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37745013-b2d8-426f-97a0-9644a8d35862)

### [Easier Copilot CLI setup](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#easier-copilot-cli-setup)

GitHub Copilot for JetBrains can now automatically install Copilot CLI from integrated terminals on macOS, Linux, and Windows. This reduces setup steps and makes it easier to start using terminal-based agent workflows directly from your IDE.

## [User experience enhancements](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#user-experience-enhancements)

This release improves common account, model, and agent interactions:

* **Account management**: Improved account management flows by supporting account switch/removal and polishing account-deletion interactions.
* **Model and settings views**: Improved model and settings usability by capping long model-name width in the model picker and refining model view/todo list panel behavior.
* **Chat references**: Restored file and folder `#` references in Copilot, Claude, and Codex chat inputs.
* **Customization**: Moved the customization button to the top of Copilot chat.
* **Agent debug logs**: Moved the agent debug logs button to the **Options** dropdown at the top of Copilot chat.

![Copilot chat showing the customization button and agent debug logs option](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dec223a8-7930-49a1-97df-8b1aa7baf2f8)

## [Quality improvements](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#quality-improvements)

This release improves reliability for MCP execution and approvals, terminal output and auto-approval, customizations, cloud agents, and diff-based editing. It also fixes ANSI escape rendering and makes terminal scrollbars more predictable.

## [Changed](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#changed)

User-facing product strings now use “Copilot” instead of “Copilot CLI.”

## [Try it out](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#try-it-out)

Try the [latest version of the GitHub Copilot plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/17718-github-copilot--your-ai-pair-programmer/versions) and share your feedback.

## [Share your feedback](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains#share-your-feedback)

Your feedback drives improvements. We’d love to hear about your experience in the following channels:

* **In-product feedback**: Use the feedback options within your IDE.
* **Feedback repository**: Share your thoughts in the [GitHub Copilot for JetBrains IDEs issues](https://github.com/microsoft/copilot-intellij-feedback/issues).

The post [Copilot memory and Ollama in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-copilot-memory-and-ollama-in-github-copilot-for-jetbrains) appeared first on [The GitHub Blog](https://github.blog).

entries.title: Automatically migrate branch protection rules to repository rulesets
entries.content:
You can now convert your existing branch protection rules to repository rulesets directly from your repository settings. This helps you migrate to GitHub’s more flexible and scalable policy framework without manually recreating each rule.

As we continue investing in rulesets as the foundation for repository governance on GitHub, this tool makes it easy to bring your existing policies forward.

### [How it works](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-automatically-migrate-branch-protection-rules-to-repository-rulesets#how-it-works)

Navigate to **Settings → Branches** in your repository, find the classic rule under **Branch protection rules**, and click **Convert to ruleset**. GitHub maps your existing branch protection configuration including required reviews, status checks, and push restrictions into equivalent ruleset rules.

[  
](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73eee67c-909e-4ed3-81aa-5a46c54f466a)

### [Why migrate to rulesets?](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-automatically-migrate-branch-protection-rules-to-repository-rulesets#why-migrate-to-rulesets)

Rulesets offer several advantages over classic branch protections:

* Apply rules across multiple branches with pattern matching.
* Layer multiple rulesets for granular policy control.
* Manage rulesets at the organization or enterprise level.
* Configure fine-grained bypass permissions for users, teams, and apps.

### [Availability](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-automatically-migrate-branch-protection-rules-to-repository-rulesets#availability)

This feature is available for all repositories where rulesets are available. [Learn more about repository rulesets](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets).

Join the discussion within [GitHub Community](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/categories/repositories).

The post [Automatically migrate branch protection rules to repository rulesets](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-11-automatically-migrate-branch-protection-rules-to-repository-rulesets) appeared first on [The GitHub Blog](https://github.blog).

entries.title: Did poop enable the evolution of complex animals?
entries.content:
The Cambrian explosion may have been fueled by poop.

The first animals on Earth emerged about 600 million years ago, and 60 million years later, those simple early animals evolved into wildly different directions, branching out into a diverse menagerie of complicated new forms and conquering new ecological niches. Known as the Cambrian Explosion, this flurry of rapid evolution produced most of the animal phyla and ecosystems we see around us today.

And it may have taken off because some of those early animals evolved a bizarre new ability: pooping. According to a recent study, the first poo pellets helped spread nutrients to deeper parts of the ocean, fueling the evolution of bigger animals in more diverse ecosystems.

[Read full article](https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/08/feces-fueled-a-flurry-of-evolution-during-the-cambrian-study-suggests/)

[Comments](https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/08/feces-fueled-a-flurry-of-evolution-during-the-cambrian-study-suggests/#comments)

entries.title: DEF CON crowd suspected in fake-hotspot attack on Delta flight
entries.content:
On Monday, passengers aboard Delta flight 591 going from Las Vegas to Atlanta allegedly spoofed the onboard Wi-Fi, raising the attention of federal law enforcement.

The incident came one day after the DEF CON security conference concluded in Las Vegas, and was first [described](https://live.acarsdrama.com/@acarsdrama/117072256729860162) on social media accounts that [follow](https://x.com/Turbinetraveler/status/2087050102930026619) publicly available air-to-ground messages, known as ACARS.

According to the “ACARS Drama” account, a message was sent by pilots from the plane stated: “NO INFO AS OF NOW WE HAVE A BUNCH OF PAX THAT WERE AT A CYBER CONFERENCE IN LAS THEY WERE ABLE TO JAM OUR WIFI AND BROADCAST THEIR SIGNAL.”

[Read full article](https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2026/08/def-con-crowd-suspected-in-fake-hotspot-attack-on-delta-flight/)

entries.title: Trump wants Big Pharma to split MMR vaccine; Big Pharma thinks it's idiotic
entries.content:
Backlash to [Trump's vaccine order on Monday](https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/08/trump-signs-bonkers-order-that-cuts-vaccines-promotes-ones-that-dont-exist/) has been swift and sharp, with various public health and medical organizations and independent experts calling it "dangerous," "[unscientific](https://news.aai.org/2026/08/11/aai-statement-on-executive-order-revising-childhood-vaccine-recommendations/)," "[false and misleading](https://www.fightinfectiousdisease.org/post/more-shots-higher-costs-no-new-data-pfid-responds-to-childhood-vaccine-executive-order)," "[so wrong](https://x.com/SenBillCassidy/status/2086906268669624512)," and saying it is "[putting children's health at risk](https://www.ama-assn.org/press-center/ama-press-releases/ama-statement-executive-order-changing-childhood-vaccine-schedule)."

The responses are unsurprising; the medical and health communities have consistently fought against the anti-vaccine, anti-science agendas pushed by Trump and his health secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has no background in science, medicine, or public health. The American Academy of Pediatrics—which called the order "[not only disheartening but dangerous](https://www.aap.org/en/news-room/news-releases/aap/2026/aap-statement-in-response-to-executive-order-on-vaccines/)"—is leading a lawsuit against previous changes to federal childhood vaccine recommendations under Trump and Kennedy. In March, the organization, along with other medical groups, [won a temporary injunction reversing most of the changes](https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/03/judge-temporarily-blocks-rfk-jr-s-changes-to-cdc-vaccine-recommendations/).

However, less expected among the scorn for Trump's order is the immediate pushback from the pharmaceutical industry.

entries.title: Scaling patterns for self-organizing multi-agent clusters with Kiro
entries.content:
Most multi-agent systems today follow the same shape: a supervisor agent breaks a task down, hands the pieces to subagents, and stitches the results back together. This is how Kiro CLI delegates to subagents, and what the Strands Agents SDK gives you primitives for with graphs and agents-as-tools. It is a good default. One process holds the plan, so behavior stays predictable and every result passes through a single gate.

That one process is also the limit. Every assignment and every result flows through the supervisor, so its context window caps how much work the system can hold at once. If it dies, the run dies with it. And because a single planner fixes the decomposition upfront, you get one take on the problem, multiplied by N workers.

Plenty of distributed systems still coordinate centrally, and should. But the alternative has been around for decades: let participants converge through shared state instead. We wanted to know what happens when you apply that move to artificial intelligence (AI) agents, so we built [kiro-flock](https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-kiro-flock), an open-source reference implementation. It runs clusters of [Kiro](https://kiro.dev) CLI agents on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) with nothing between them but an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. No orchestrator, no message bus. Agents coordinate by reading each other’s append-only logs. This post explains the pattern and gives you enough to deploy the sample and watch a cluster converge yourself.

## When to use this pattern

Architecture has to match the task. In the 2025 study “Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems” of 260 agent-system configurations they found exactly that: task performance ran from +80.8 percent on decomposable financial  
 reasoning to -70.0 percent on sequential planning, against a single-agent baseline.  
 Neither the supervisor nor this pattern wins everywhere.

A self-organizing cluster fits work that splits into many quasi-independent contributions toward one goal: reviewing a large code base, migrating hundreds of modules against a known target, generating tests or design alternatives at scale. It also suits brainstorming where you want real variety instead of one planner’s take. Parallelism matters more than ordering. Agents can join, fail, and leave without ceremony.

A supervisor fits the opposite profile. The task tree is known upfront, steps depend on each other, or you need a verification gate before results ship. The same study found that architectures without centralized verification propagate more errors. That is a real cost of removing the arbiter, though you can still gate the finished result the way the migration example ends in a full test pass. What a cluster will not give you is a gate between every step, and if you need that, the supervisor earns its bottleneck.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Workload profile** | **Better fit** |
| Many independent contributions, one goal | Cluster |
| Decomposition should emerge from the work | Cluster |
| Diversity of approaches is an asset | Cluster |
| Long-running, agents come and go | Cluster |
| Known task tree, strict ordering | Supervisor |
| Central verification gate required | Supervisor |
| Interactive, latency-sensitive | Supervisor |

## The pattern

The core decision: coordination lives in shared state. No component plans, assigns, or aggregates for the rest. Three parts make it work:

* **Agents.** Independent processes that read and write a shared store and never connect to each other. One agent failing stops only its own log.
* **A shared environment.** A single store holds a direction file, one append-only log per agent, and a working area for artifacts.
* **A direction.** A markdown file that states the goal and leaves the path to the agents.

Each agent runs a loop. It starts a fresh session, reads the direction and the logs of a bounded set of peers, decides on one contribution that moves the goal forward, writes its artifacts, and appends one line to its own log:

```
{"ts":"2026-07-21T14:12:42Z","iteration":0,"action":"wrote discussion on coordination topologies","result":"Created discussion-coordination-topologies.md covering ring vs mesh vs swarm trade-offs with analysis of convergence/diversity tension.","next_intent":"read neighbour contributions and either deepen topology discussion or explore a second angle"}
```

That line is the entire coordination message. No broker delivers it, no acknowledgment comes back. The next agent that reads it decides for itself what to do about it. Remove an agent and its neighbors read one fewer log. Add one mid-run and it joins the division of labor already underway.

The bounded peer set is deliberate. Agents sit in a logical ring and each reads a fixed number of neighbors on either side, set by a radius parameter. Give every agent full visibility and the cluster collapses onto whatever the first agent wrote, because each later agent reads that as consensus. Limited visibility lets signals spread gradually, and agents working from different context get room to develop alternatives.

In kiro-flock, each agent is a [headless Kiro CLI](https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/headless/) session on its own Amazon EC2 instance, and the shared environment is an Amazon S3 bucket. Which tools an agent may use without review, and what each iteration reads and writes, are design decisions you make once per cluster. We think of them as harness engineering and loop engineering, and the drift failure mode in the following section shows why the fresh session per iteration matters.

## What a run looks like

![Reference architecture: EC2 agent instances, an S3 shared environment holding the direction, logs, and artifacts, an API Gateway and Lambda control plane behind Amazon Cognito, CloudWatch metrics, and Amazon Bedrock post-run analysis.](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fc074d501302eb2b93e2554793fcaf50b3bf7291/2026/08/11/ARCHBLOG-1576-1.png)

Figure 1. Reference architecture for a kiro-flock cluster on AWS.

  
 Agents run as headless Kiro CLI sessions on EC2 instances, each reading and writing the S3 bucket that holds the direction, one log per agent, and the shared artifacts. An Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda control plane behind Amazon Cognito starts, stops, and steers clusters from the dashboard. Agents publish metrics to Amazon CloudWatch, and Amazon Bedrock backs the post-run analysis.

Take a concrete run: sixteen agents in a ring, directed to hold a distributed discussion on AI agent clustering and converge on a shared synthesis. The operator writes one direction file and starts the cluster. Nothing else is assigned.

The following lines are from that run (result fields shortened for print). In the first iteration the agents fanned out with no assignment: failure modes, coordination topologies, distributed-systems parallels, and several overlapping stigmergy pieces, all written in parallel within one minute of start. The later lines show an agent correcting course after reading its neighbors, the synthesis forming, and the cluster winding itself down:

```
{"ts":"2026-07-21T14:12:42Z","iteration":0,"action":"wrote discussion-failure-modes.md","result":"covered 5 failure modes (premature convergence, echo chambers, hot-spot collapse, idle cascades, stale reads) with mitigations","next_intent":"read neighbours next iteration, look for topics to challenge or extend"}
{"ts":"2026-07-21T14:14:31Z","iteration":1,"action":"wrote discussion-scaling-laws.md","result":"explored scaling regimes and communication cost vs value; diverged from neighbours who all wrote stigmergy in iteration 0","next_intent":"read neighbour updates, check if any uncovered angles remain"}
{"ts":"2026-07-21T14:16:04Z","iteration":2,"action":"wrote synthesis.md","result":"structured synthesis: 5 core claims, 3 key tensions, 5 open questions; integrated topologies, scaling, economics, failure modes","next_intent":"read neighbours' reactions to synthesis, refine, move toward idle if coverage is solid"}
{"ts":"2026-07-21T14:22:24Z","iteration":7,"action":"idle","result":"All 6 visible neighbours idle (iterations 4-6). Synthesis.md stable and comprehensive. Direction unchanged. Cluster fully converged.","next_intent":"remain idle unless direction changes or operator requests further work"}
```

The cluster converged on a shared synthesis covering the angles in the direction, and by iteration 7 all sixteen agents had declared themselves idle. Nobody assigned the topics, arbitrated the synthesis, or told the cluster it was done. Even done is only a signal read from the logs, since an agent goes idle when its neighbors are idle and the output is stable.

![kiro-flock dashboard showing a single six-agent cluster running the amorphous algorithm at radius 1, each agent card listing its neighbors, health, and iteration log, with the shared environment and direction on the right.](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fc074d501302eb2b93e2554793fcaf50b3bf7291/2026/08/11/ARCHBLOG-1576-2.png)

Figure 2. A single cluster in the kiro-flock dashboard. Six agents run at radius 1, each on its own EC2 instance. Every agent card shows its neighbors and its latest log line, the “did / result / next intent” message its neighbors read. The right panel shows the shared environment in S3 and the direction the cluster works toward.

## Three ways to answer “whose work do I read?”

Every iteration starts with that question, and the answer defines the coordination algorithm. kiro-flock ships three, swappable at runtime.

**Amorphous (ring).** Each agent reads a fixed window of neighbors set by radius R. An agent at radius 2 reads four neighbors whether the cluster holds 8 agents or 800, so per-agent work stays constant as the cluster grows. The ceiling is your EC2 vCPU quota, not the algorithm. The largest system we have run so far totaled 184 agents across 11 cooperating clusters, creating a programming language. Rings beyond the low hundreds are extrapolation from that constant per-agent cost, not tested territory. The price is speed: a signal moves one hop per iteration. That slowness is also what lets dissenting agents mature alternatives before the neighborhood locks in. Use it for parallel work, or as the opening phase before consensus.

**Mesh (full visibility).** Every agent reads every other agent’s latest entry. Alignment is fast and context grows linearly with the cluster, so mesh stays comfortable to about 30 agents and workable to about 50. Diversity collapses, because agents reacting to the same first signal agree instead of exploring. Use it when a small group must converge quickly.

**Swarm (recency).** Each agent reads the K most recently active peers, so the cluster reorganizes around where the action is. Good for ideation, runs well past 100 agents. If K stays small while N grows, most agents read the same few peers and pile onto one subtask. Raise K or switch to amorphous.

A productive sequence uses all three: open amorphous to explore, switch to swarm as a direction forms, finish in mesh to align on the output.

How long does convergence take? In a ring, one iteration carries a signal 2R positions, so full propagation takes ceil(N / 2R) iterations, and consensus roughly two to three times that, because agents observe, react, and confirm. The wall-clock column assumes an iteration interval of 30 seconds per agent loop, the default interval in the reference implementation. The interval is configurable per cluster.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Agents (N)** | **Radius (R)** | **Propagation ceil(N/2R)** | **Consensus (2-3x)** | **Wall clock to propagate** |
| 8 | 1 | 4 iterations | 8-12 iterations | about 2 minutes |
| 100 | 2 | 25 iterations | 50-75 iterations | about 12 minutes |
| 1,000 | 4 | 125 iterations | 250-375 iterations | about 62 minutes |
| 1,000 | 20 | 25 iterations | 50-75 iterations | about 12 minutes |

Radius trades per-agent context for convergence speed, as the last two rows show. For parallel map-style work, propagation barely matters. Agents only need to avoid duplicating each other. It costs you when the task needs consensus, so match radius and cluster size to the context you are in. The cost model follows the same logic: no always-on orchestrator and no broker. You pay for Kiro credits and the EC2 instances while they run, plus S3 storage and requests. You also pay for the AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and Amazon Bedrock usage the control plane and post-run analysis incur. See [AWS Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/pricing/).

None of this is new theory. Identical unreliable parts producing coherent global behavior through local reads is amorphous computing. Coordinating through traces left in a shared medium instead of messages is stigmergy, described by Grassé for termites in 1959 and formalized for artificial systems by Theraulaz and Bonabeau. And a set of append-only logs is a grow-only conflict-free replicated data type (CRDT) spreading gossip-style: replicas converge without locks, which is all the consistency this workload needs.

## Where it breaks

Self-organizing clusters fail in ways orchestrated systems do not. With no supervisor to arbitrate, a bad signal can spread before anyone corrects it. Four failure modes recur, and each maps to a design choice rather than a safeguard bolted on afterward.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Failure mode** | **Where it comes from** | **Design choice that addresses it** |
| Groupthink | Mesh visibility collapses the cluster onto the first signal | Open amorphous to build diversity, switch to mesh only to align |
| Drift | Persistent session history builds behavioral momentum | Fresh session per iteration. State lives only in shared logs |
| Hot spots | Swarm with K too small for N starves subtasks | Raise K, or switch to amorphous |
| Carry-over | Stale files from a previous run read as current context | Archive environment/ and store/ to history/ on every start |

Drift deserves one more sentence, because it is the least obvious. An agent that keeps its session history carries a narrow reading of the direction forward even after its neighbors move on. Starting every iteration with no conversational memory sounds wasteful. It is actually the control that keeps a thousand independent loops steerable. The only state an agent carries is what it reads back from the shared logs.

## Composing clusters

The same decision works one level up: clusters coordinate by reading each other’s shared environment, the way agents read each other’s logs. We run a structure we call WeltenBuilder: a feature cluster implements against an agreed interface, a shared-infrastructure cluster owns common services, a QA cluster reads across the others and reports inconsistencies as artifacts. A coordinator cluster writes conflict-resolution notes the others pick up on their next iteration. A resolution note is a trace, not a command. Remove the coordinator and you remove a signal, not a dependency.

Because the shared environment is the coordination plane, all clusters launch at the same time with no dependency graph to sequence. Contract bottlenecks dissolve the same way: a small mesh cluster converges on interface definitions in a few iterations while other clusters build against its latest stable output. This is where the pattern points: standing clusters, each producing one class of artifact, composed into a factory whose unit of work is a direction file and a topology.

![kiro-flock WeltenBuilder dashboard showing several specialized clusters running at once, each with its own algorithm and agent count, beside the shared environment tree on the right.](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fc074d501302eb2b93e2554793fcaf50b3bf7291/2026/08/11/ARCHBLOG-1576-3.png)

Figure 3. Multiple specialized clusters in the WeltenBuilder dashboard, each with its own algorithm and agent count, coordinating only through the shared S3 environment on the right.

## Try it

The [kiro-flock](https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-kiro-flock) reference implementation is open source under Apache 2.0. It is a sample to study and adapt, not a production system.

One setup script provisions the stack with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK): Amazon S3 for the shared environment, Amazon EC2 for the agents, and AWS Lambda with Amazon API Gateway as a control plane behind a dashboard. The dashboard starts and stops clusters, changes the algorithm, and updates the direction mid-run. Amazon Cognito handles access, and Amazon Bedrock backs a post-run analysis that summarizes how the cluster converged.

You need an AWS account with the AWS CDK bootstrapped. Install [kiro-cli](https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/installation/) and create a Kiro API key for headless mode (requires a Kiro subscription). Then:

```
cp install.config.template install.config   # set REGION and PROFILE
./setup.sh
```

Direct a cluster in plain language: “Start a flock of 8 agents to review the files in my project and suggest improvements.” The default runs 8 agents at radius 1 and converged in 5 to 7 iterations in our runs. Before wider use, scope each agent’s EC2 AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role, restrict security-group egress to the endpoints agents should call, and add AWS Budgets alerts.

## Conclusion

The supervisor pattern remains the right default for bounded task trees, whether you build it with Strands, Kiro CLI subagents, or any of the coding agents that delegate this way. When the work decomposes into many independent contributions and diversity matters more than a central gate, moving coordination into shared state helps remove the throughput ceiling and the single point of failure in one move. The convergence math and the failure modes both follow from that decision, and the distributed-systems results they rest on have been known for decades. Deploy the sample, read the logs as a cluster converges, and decide where your own multi-agent workloads belong.
